reviews.topic: host-supplied targets, ID matching, and no path opening
reviews.source_evidence: EC3 §8.10.4.1 physical 290-291 / printed 275-276: Table 95 requires /F and makes /ID optional; /ID improves chances of finding intended file. §14.4 says both IDs matching makes it very likely the correct unchanged file was found, while matching only first identifies a different version of the correct file. Table 95 does not say that /ID is required for locating the target.
reviews.current_code_evidence: The host reads every file from a user-selected directory and passes bytes/names. `Supply::find` ignores FileSpec and requires an ID; `Supply::read` rejects PDFs with no ID. The document cannot cause arbitrary path opening, which is a sound host-trust boundary; however, an explicitly supplied /F-matching file with no ID cannot be imported, and candidate selection with duplicate permanent IDs is first-match order rather than exact-pair/FileSpec resolution.
reviews.verdict: Keep the security policy that the renderer itself never opens a document-selected path. Reopen the narrower matching decision: distinguish the host-authorized supplied set from arbitrary filesystem access, and decide whether supplied-name /F matching is a supported fallback when ID is absent. For multiple permanent-ID matches, source gives identity evidence but no explicit search-priority algorithm; do not assert the exact-pair-first rule as unambiguous until owner/source interpretation resolves it.
reviews.limits: A host's chosen directory may intentionally be a collection of candidates; /F may include device-specific paths or relative subpaths. The assignment has not established how those map safely to host names. Embedded target support is a separate branch: source permits embedding, but this reader has no current internal supply route.

reviews.topic: imported page as its own group under proxy group
reviews.source_evidence: §8.10.4.1 physical 291 / printed 276 requires proxy Group attrs apply to imported page; §11.4.7 addresses target page's own group.
reviews.verdict: No reversal proposed. ADR distinguishes the two dictionary scopes, and the current reference_xobjects tests include source-derived group controls. This shard did not re-certify the group matrix.

reviews.source_evidence: §8.10.4.2 physical 291 / printed 276 is explicitly permissive and names two allowed outputs dependent on capabilities, preferences, and job nature.
reviews.verdict: The code's choice to print imported content when the host supplied a target, otherwise proxy, is permitted; no mandatory output-choice defect. Ledger test attribution is too broad: its cited print test verifies job resolution, not reference-object output. Add the public seam test in drafts to show the selected implementation behavior and its no-supply control, without treating one allowed choice as mandated conformance.

No separate contradiction found. The print clause is a permission exercised by the product, so it can be tracked as implemented if the selected choice is observable; the source's permission does not require both outputs.
